title: Group singing 'Down on the Farm'; Charlie Lawrence in the band
summary: Howard says the whole band sang 'Down on the Farm', he sang no solos, and Charlie Lawrence played piano and was starting to arrange.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: He said, we were all singing. I want to know about that.
Yeah, 'Down on the Farm.'
Everybody in the band was singing.
Yeah.
So you did a lot of group singing.
Wasn't too good, but we were singing. 'Down on the Farm.'
That was when Lionel was in there.
Yeah.
Because he did a lot of singing later, with his band, didn't he?
Yeah.
Would you rehearse the singing or was it just something that --
Yeah, we'd rehearse it. Everybody was singing that 'Down on the Farm' thing -- what was the name of that -- oh, I can't sing it no more.
What about you doing individual singing, did you ever do any vocals where you were singing alone?
No, not alone. I didn't do no singing alone.
Let's see, was Lawrence in this band? Charles was in there (unintelligible)
Lloyd Reese?
No, Lloyd Reese was in one of the bands there, but Charles Lawrence.
Charlie Lawrence?
Yes, Charlie Lawrence.
Oh, Charlie was in the band, but he didn't sing.
Was he an arranger at that period too, Charlie Lawrence?
No, he was getting to be an arranger, though. He got a lot of them in.
What do you think, anything else?
